description: Phase 6: Add sort order management — auto-populate sort_order on artist assignment, prompt sort order via Telegram after show IG publish with ⬆️/⬇️ inline buttons, handle reorder callbacks.

steps.task: Add `set_artist_sort_order` helper in db.rs: `pub async fn set_artist_sort_order(pool: &SqlitePool, show_id: i64, artist_id: i64, new_order: i32) -> Result<(), sqlx::Error>`. Updates `UPDATE artist_show_assignments SET sort_order = ? WHERE show_id = ? AND artist_id = ?`.

Auto-populate sort_order when assigning an artist to a show. In the show assignment handler in api.rs (search for INSERT INTO artist_show_assignments): after inserting the row, count existing assignments for the show and set sort_order to the count (making it the last position). Or better: set sort_order in the INSERT itself: `INSERT INTO artist_show_assignments (artist_id, show_id, sort_order) VALUES (?, ?, (SELECT COALESCE(MAX(sort_order), -1) + 1 FROM artist_show_assignments WHERE show_id = ?))`.

decisions: Use subquery in INSERT to compute next sort_order — atomic, no race condition
COALESCE handles case when no assignments exist yet (returns 0)
learnings: Show assignment is handled in api.rs around lines 576-629

steps.task: Add `send_sort_order_prompt` function in telegram_notify.rs (or telegram.rs). Takes (state, show_id). Fetches artists assigned to the show ordered by sort_order,name. Sends a message to the Telegram topic listing artists with their current order and ⬆️/⬇️ inline buttons. Each artist gets one row with buttons: [⬆️ callback_data=aig_sort:{show_id}:{artist_id}:up] [Name (position N)] [⬇️ callback_data=aig_sort:{show_id}:{artist_id}:down]. First artist has no ⬆️, last has no ⬇️. Caption: '📋 Set artist post order for {show_title}\n\nDay 1 after show → first artist, Day 2 → second, etc.'

decisions: Use inline keyboard with ⬆️/⬇️ buttons per artist row
First artist omits ⬆️, last omits ⬇️ (can't move beyond bounds)
learnings: Telegram InlineKeyboardMarkup supports multiple rows, each row is an array of button objects
knowledge.notes: This message is sent as a text message with inline keyboard (not a photo), so use bot.send_message or a raw JSON POST to sendMessage with reply_markup

steps.task: Trigger sort order prompt after show IG publish. In `cmd_post_show_instagram` in telegram.rs (line ~621): after successful publish, call `send_sort_order_prompt(state, show_id)`. This asks the user to set the order for upcoming artist preview posts.

decisions: Only trigger after successful publish (not on failure)
learnings: cmd_post_show_instagram is at line 621 of telegram.rs
knowledge.notes: Also consider triggering from the API handler (api_post_show_to_instagram) for admin dashboard publishes

steps.task: Implement `handle_aig_sort` callback handler in telegram.rs. On callback data `aig_sort:{show_id}:{artist_id}:{direction}`: (1) Parse show_id, artist_id, direction ('up' or 'down'). (2) Fetch all artists for the show ordered by sort_order,name. (3) Find the target artist's current position. (4) Find the adjacent artist (above for 'up', below for 'down'). (5) Swap their sort_order values using two UPDATE queries. (6) Re-render the sort order message by calling editMessageReplyMarkup with the updated inline keyboard. (7) Wire this into the callback query dispatcher from Phase 1 step 6.

decisions: Swap sort_order values between adjacent artists (not shift all)
Re-render the entire inline keyboard after swap to reflect new order
knowledge.notes: Use editMessageText (not editMessageReplyMarkup) if we also want to update the text showing the new order. Or use editMessageReplyMarkup if only the buttons change.

steps.task: Run `cargo check` from source/backend/ to verify Phase 6 compiles. Fix any compilation errors.
